## Overview

While `generate_report()` bundles everything into one HTML file, every plot
and table in NanoQuRe is also available as a standalone function. This is
useful when you want to embed a specific plot in your own R Markdown report,
tweak parameters, or inspect a single metric interactively.

```{r load-data}
library(NanoQuRe)

data(sample_data)
```

---

## Summary tables

### `sequencing_stats()`

Returns a one-row summary of the run: duration, total bases sequenced,
pass rate, and average translocation speed.

```{r sequencing-stats}
sequencing_stats(sample_data)
```

### `quality_stats()`

Returns key quality metrics: total and passed read counts, N50, mean Q score,
longest read, and mean length of passed reads.

```{r quality-stats}
quality_stats(sample_data)
```

---

## Yield plots

### `plot_cumulative_yield()`

Shows how total sequenced bases accumulate over the run, split by pass/fail
status. A flattening curve indicates the run is winding down.

```{r cumulative-yield}
plot_cumulative_yield(sample_data)
```

### `plot_seq_throughput()`

Shows yield per hour rather than cumulative yield — useful for spotting
periods of low pore activity or blockages during the run.

```{r seq-throughput}
plot_seq_throughput(sample_data)
```

---

## Speed

### `plot_average_speed()`

Shows the average translocation speed of DNA through the pore in bases per
second, split by pass/fail. A drop in speed can indicate pore aging or
buffer issues.

```{r average-speed}
plot_average_speed(sample_data)
```

---

## Read length distribution

### `plot_read_lengths()`

Plots a histogram of read lengths on a log10 axis, with vertical lines for
the mean read length and the N50 value. By default each bar is the number of
reads in a length bin; `weight = "bases"` shows the number of bases instead,
i.e. where the sequenced bases are. `upper_limit` sets the x axis maximum;
reads beyond it are counted in a note on the plot. `log_x = FALSE` switches
to a linear axis.

```{r read-lengths}
plot_read_lengths(sample_data)
```

```{r read-lengths-custom, eval = FALSE}
# bases per length bin, on a linear axis up to 20 kb
plot_read_lengths(sample_data, weight = "bases", log_x = FALSE, upper_limit = 20000)
```

---

## Quality distribution

### `plot_quality_distribution()`

Plots the Q score distribution split by pass/fail. Two vertical lines are
shown: the basecaller's own pass/fail threshold (derived from the data) and
a user-defined cutoff for downstream analysis.

```{r quality-distribution}
# default user-defined cutoff is Q7
plot_quality_distribution(sample_data, qscore_cutoff = 7)
```

---

## Channel activity

### `plot_active_channels()`

Shows how many channels produced at least one read in each time window
(10 minutes by default, set with `bin_width` in hours). Dashed lines mark
the first window in which this number falls to 50% and 25% of the highest
count in the first hour. Pore scans and pauses are not recorded in the
sequencing summary, so short dips or gaps can reflect run control rather
than pore loss.

```{r active-channels}
plot_active_channels(sample_data)
```

### `pore_activity_heatmap()`

Shows two complementary views of pore activity: a time × channel heatmap
and a spatial heatmap overlaid on the flowcell layout. Darker colour means
more bases sequenced through that channel.

```{r pore-heatmap}
pore_activity_heatmap(sample_data, platform = "minion")
```

---

## N50 directly

### `calculate_n50()`

If you just need the N50 value without any plot:

```{r n50}
calculate_n50(sample_data)
```
